Register a condathis backend

Source: R/backend.R
register_backend.Rd

Adds a backend: the engine that creates Conda environments and runs commands in them. condathis has one built-in backend, "micromamba". Another package can provide a backend and register it from its .onLoad() (see Registering from a backend package). The backend's name is then a valid method value of every condathis function that takes method, and method = "auto" can select it.

Usage

register_backend(name, backend, call = rlang::caller_env())

Arguments

name

Character string, the backend name that users pass as method. It must start with a letter, contain only letters, digits, ., _ and -, and not end with .. It must not be a Windows device name, such as "nul", "con" or "com1", with or without an extension. Reserved, in any case: "auto", "native" and "micromamba", the names of the entries of the condathis data directory ("envs", "pkgs", "micromamba", "condabin", "Scripts", "condathis-micromamba.yaml", "cache", "home", "channels" and "locks"), and "tmp", "bin", "lib", "etc" and "conda-meta". register_backend() also refuses a name when the condathis data directory has an entry of that name that is not a directory. It also refuses a name that differs only in case from a registered backend name or from the backend name of a package that condathis knows, such as "rattler". On macOS and Windows, both would have the same root. Registering a name again replaces its backend.

backend

The backend object: a list of the backend functions, with its own class. See The backend object.

call

The environment reported as the caller in errors, for calls from another package's .onLoad(), as in rlang.

Value

name, invisibly. Aborts with these classes:

  • condathis_backend_invalid_name: a name that breaks the rules above.

  • condathis_backend_reserved_name (also condathis_backend_invalid_name): a reserved name.

  • condathis_backend_root_conflict (also condathis_backend_invalid_name): a name whose entry in the condathis data directory is not a directory.

  • condathis_backend_name_conflict (also condathis_backend_invalid_name): a name that differs only in case from another backend name.

  • condathis_backend_class_conflict: another registered name uses the same first class.

  • condathis_backend_contract_violation: a backend object that breaks the contract. The error names the missing functions or arguments.

Every error also has the class condathis_error, and the name errors have condathis_invalid_arg.

Details

backend is a list of backend functions, with its own class: the three required functions described below, and any of the optional ones. condathis supplies a default for every optional function that the list leaves out. register_backend() checks the list, then registers each function as an S3 method of the condathis generic of the same name, from inside the condathis namespace. The backend package needs no S3 registrations in its NAMESPACE.

Lifecycle

This extension API is experimental. condathis 0.2.0 defines the contract, designed together with a second backend package (rattlerthis). The API may still change in breaking ways between 0.x releases. State the condathis version that you developed against, for example as condathis (>= 0.2.0) in Imports.

The backend object

Build the backend as:

structure(
  list(<the functions>),
  class = c("condathis_backend_<name>", "condathis_backend")
)

S3 dispatch keys on the first class, so it must be unique to the backend. It must not be "condathis_backend", "default", "list" or "data.frame": methods for those classes would also catch objects that are not this backend. The element names are the names of the functions below. The object must have backend_create_env, backend_install and backend_resolve_run. Each other function is optional: an element that is missing or NULL gets the default of condathis. Each function must accept every argument of its signature by name, or have a ... argument. register_backend() checks the class and the three required functions. It checks that each other element of the contract is a function or NULL. It also checks the rule of the next paragraph and the arguments of the functions that are present. Extra elements are ignored.

An object that has its own backend_get_install_dir() must also have its own backend_get_env_dir(), backend_list_envs() and backend_env_exists(). An object that has its own backend_get_env_dir() must also have its own backend_list_envs() and backend_env_exists(). Their defaults look for environments in <backend_root_dir(name)>/envs, not where the backend keeps them.

Roots

Each backend has a root, its data directory, which get_install_dir() reports. The root of the "micromamba" backend is the condathis data directory, tools::R_user_dir("condathis", "data"). The root of every other backend is the directory of its name inside it, backend_root_dir(): for example <condathis data directory>/rattler. So the root of a backend can lie inside the root of micromamba. The names of the entries of the condathis data directory are reserved (see name). Each backend has its own environment directory, <root>/envs, and its own package caches, and never uses those of another backend. condathis owns <root>/conda-pkgs in the root of every backend (see Child processes), so a backend must not use that name. with_sandbox_dir() moves the condathis data directory, and with it every root that backend_root_dir() gives.

What condathis passes

condathis passes backend first and every other argument by name. It checks every value before it calls a backend function. verbose is always one of the five strings, so the defaults of the signatures below are never used. The values are:

  • backend: the registered backend object.

  • env_name: a valid environment name, as described for the env_name argument of create_env(). It is a single directory name, never a path.

  • packages: a character vector of package match specs, such as "python>=3.12", without NA or "". backend_create_env() gets NULL when the request has no packages: an empty environment, or one built from env_file. backend_install() gets NULL when it installs from env_file.

  • env_file: NULL, or the absolute path of an existing environment file (or directory) from an env_definition(). When it is set, packages is NULL.

  • definition: the env_definition() object that env_file comes from, a list with path (the same path as env_file), format (NULL or a string) and options (a named list). It came after the first functions of version 2 of this contract, so it is not in the signatures below, and a function written without it keeps working. condathis passes it only to a function that has a definition argument (or ...), and only when env_file is set. condathis never reads format or options: the backend does. A backend function without the argument gets only env_file. Then a definition with a format or options aborts before any call, with class condathis_create_env_unsupported_definition or condathis_install_packages_unsupported_definition (also condathis_backend_unsupported).

  • channels: a non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, without NA or "", in priority order.

  • additional_channels: NULL, or a character vector like channels. These channels come after channels.

  • channel_priority: "strict", "flexible" or "disabled".

  • platform: NULL, or one known conda platform (subdir) name, such as "linux-64" or "osx-arm64" (see platform in create_env()). It can still be a platform that the backend does not support. NULL means the native platform of the backend.

  • overwrite: TRUE or FALSE.

  • verbose: one of "output" (show the backend's output), "silent" (show nothing), "cmd" (show the command line), "spinner" (show only progress) or "full" (show everything, also the backend's own log). It is never a logical or a vector. The probes and listings that condathis uses to choose a backend get "silent". condathis prints its own messages, such as "Environment x successfully created.", so the backend must not print them again.

  • cmd: a single, non-empty string. args: a character vector.

  • base_env: a named character vector, the environment of the command before activation (see backend_resolve_run()).

  • env_dir: the absolute path of an existing directory with a conda-meta directory, in its real form (see backend_resolve_run_in_dir()).

  • timeout: a positive number of seconds. It can also be Inf (no limit) for backend_resolve_run() and backend_resolve_run_in_dir().

create_env(), install_packages() and remove_env() hold the lock of the environment name (see Other R sessions in create_env()). They hold it while they call backend_create_env(), backend_install() or backend_remove_env(), and during the existence checks before them. So no other R session that uses condathis changes the environment meanwhile, with any backend. They also hold the lock of the package caches, shared. clean_cache() holds it exclusive while it calls backend_clean_cache(). So no create or install of another R session runs while caches are deleted. A backend needs no lock of its own against those sessions.

Required functions

  • backend_create_env(backend, packages = NULL, env_file = NULL, env_name = "condathis-env", channels = "conda-forge", channel_priority = c("strict", "flexible", "disabled"), additional_channels = NULL, platform = NULL, overwrite = FALSE, verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full")) creates the environment. It can also take the optional argument definition = NULL (see What condathis passes). Its directory is the one that backend_get_env_dir() returns, and condathis calls it only when that directory does not exist. That is the case for a new environment. It is also the case with overwrite = TRUE, after condathis moved the existing environment aside or deleted a directory that was not an environment (one left by a failed create). When the call fails, condathis deletes what it left and moves the old environment back. A call fails also when it returns a non-zero status or an invalid link_scripts_skipped (see Results). So a misspelled spec with overwrite = TRUE does not cost the user the environment. overwrite tells the backend which of the two cases applies. With env_file, build the environment from that file (read definition for its format and options, when the function takes it). With platform, build it for that platform. The platform can be one that condathis chose because the request does not solve for the native platform of the backend (see backend_can_solve()). After a successful call, condathis writes <env_dir>/.condathis/backend.json. It uses this marker as a cross-check, and the marker records the platform when one was given or chosen.

    condathis moves aside or deletes only the directory
    <backend_get_install_dir()>/envs/<env_name>. For a backend whose backend_get_env_dir() returns another directory, create_env() cannot replace an existing environment, or delete a directory left by a failed create. It aborts with condathis_create_env_failed, whose parent has the class condathis_unsafe_env_dir_move or condathis_unsafe_env_dir_delete.

    condathis keeps the environment that it replaces in the directory
    <backend_get_install_dir()>/envs/#trash until the backend succeeded. No environment can have that name, so backend_list_envs() must leave that directory out.

  • backend_install(backend, packages, env_name = "condathis-env", channels = "conda-forge", channel_priority = c("strict", "flexible", "disabled"), additional_channels = NULL, platform = NULL, verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full")) installs packages into the existing environment env_name, solving for platform. condathis passes the platform recorded for the environment: the one in its marker or its .mambarc. On Apple Silicon and on Windows, condathis can choose an emulated platform (see backend_can_solve()). There it also reads the platform of the package records of an environment without a recorded one. For an environment without packages of a platform, it passes the platform that it would choose for a new environment. Otherwise, platform is NULL. It must not create a missing environment.

    It can also take the optional arguments env_file = NULL and definition = NULL. With env_file, install the packages that the file requests, solved together with the packages of the environment, as micromamba install -f does. install_packages() passes a file only when backend_describe_definition() did not say that it is a lock (or that the backend cannot read it). A function that takes neither argument cannot install from a file, and install_packages() then aborts before any call with class condathis_install_packages_unsupported_definition. A function that takes env_file but not definition gets only the path, as backend_create_env() does.

  • backend_resolve_run(backend, cmd, args = character(0L), env_name = "condathis-env", verbose = "silent", base_env = NULL, timeout = Inf) describes, without running cmd, how to run cmd with args in the activated environment. base_env is the environment that the command gets without activation: the session's environment with the changes of Child processes. Compute the activation against it, not against the environment of the R session. condathis always passes it. timeout is the number of seconds the function may take: what is left of the timeout of run(), run_bin() or run_pipeline(), or Inf. If the function runs code to compute the activation, such as the activate.d scripts of the environment, that code can hang. The function should stop it when the time runs out, and signal an error. When the time ran out, condathis reports a timeout for the call (timeout = TRUE, status -9), whatever the function returned or signaled. It does not start the command. timeout is the one argument a function may leave out. Then condathis does not pass it, and can report the timeout only once the function returned. The function returns list(command, args, env, dir):

    • command: a single string, the program to start: an absolute path, or a bare name. condathis starts a bare name the same way for every backend. On Linux and macOS, it is looked up on the PATH of the command, after env is applied. On Windows, run() and run_pipeline() look it up in the binary directories of the environment, with the extensions of PATHEXT. Otherwise, they leave it to processx, which searches the working directory and the PATH of the R session for <name>.com and <name>.exe. run_bin() searches the binary directories of the environment and then the PATH of the command. A bare name that is found nowhere fails to start.

    • args: a character vector, or NULL. It replaces the user's arguments, so it must contain them.

    • env: NULL, or a named character vector (not a list) of activation variables. Each entry replaces the variable of the same name in the environment of the command, PATH included. An NA entry removes the variable, for a variable that the activation unsets. run_bin() also prepends the environment's binary directories to PATH.

    • dir: NULL to keep R's working directory, or the path of an existing directory to run the command in.

    condathis calls it only with activation on (run(), and run_bin() and run_pipeline() with activate = TRUE). It calls it only for an environment that this backend reported as existing. It never calls it for an env_path() environment (see backend_resolve_run_in_dir()). A value that breaks these rules aborts with condathis_backend_resolve_run_invalid.

Optional functions and their defaults

The defaults treat the environments of a backend as conda prefixes in <backend_root_dir(name)>/envs. A directory there with conda-meta/history is an environment, and the conda-meta/*.json files are its package records.

  • backend_get_install_dir(backend) returns the backend's root: the absolute path of an existing directory, in its real form (fs::path_real()). Paths then compare equal where a temporary directory is a symbolic link (macOS). Create the directory when it is missing. Default: backend_root_dir(), created when missing.

  • backend_get_env_dir(backend, env_name = "condathis-env") returns the absolute path of the environment directory (its prefix): the directory that backend_create_env() creates. It returns the path also for an environment that does not exist yet, and it must not create anything. Default: <backend_root_dir(name)>/envs/<env_name>.

  • backend_list_envs(backend, verbose = "silent") returns the names of this backend's environments: a character vector without NA or duplicates. Names of the vector are dropped. It returns character(0) when there are none, also when the backend's root does not exist yet. It is read only: it must not create anything, and it should not install or download anything. Default: the directories in <root>/envs that have conda-meta/history, without symbolic links and without directories whose real path is elsewhere, as micromamba env list reports them.

  • backend_env_exists(backend, env_name, verbose = "silent") returns TRUE or FALSE: whether env_name is an environment of this backend. It must agree with backend_list_envs(). condathis calls it for every registered backend on every call that names an environment, whatever method is, to find the backend that owns the environment. So it must be cheap and must not create anything. Avoid processes and downloads. Report only the environments in this backend's own root: when two backends report the same name, condathis aborts with condathis_backend_ambiguous_env unless method names one of them. Default: FALSE when <root>/envs/<env_name> is not a directory, else whether backend_list_envs() lists env_name (a file system that ignores case opens the directory for every spelling).

  • backend_list_packages(backend, env_name = "condathis-env", verbose = "silent") returns a data frame (a tibble is fine) with one row per installed package and at least these columns: name, version, build_string, channel and platform (character), and build_number (integer, or a double with whole numbers). platform is the subdir of the package, such as "linux-64" or "noarch". Extra columns are kept. An empty environment gives zero rows with the same columns. create_env() reads these columns to decide whether an existing environment already has the requested packages and was built for the requested platform. Default: the package records, with the columns of micromamba list --json, and the PyPI packages that pip or uv installed into the environment's python, as micromamba list lists them (channel pypi, and as platform a tag such as linux-x86_64). See list_packages().

  • backend_remove_env(backend, env_name = "condathis-env", verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full")) removes the environment and its directory. Default: deletes conda-meta/history first, so the environment leaves every listing at once. Then it moves the directory into <root>/envs/#trash and deletes it there. When a program uses one of its files (Windows), the directory cannot be moved. Then it deletes the files one by one, and moves each file in use into #trash, where a later call deletes it. A symbolic link is deleted, never followed. It does not run pre-unlink scripts, and reports the packages that have one (see Results). Like create_env(), it deletes only the directory <backend_get_install_dir()>/envs/<env_name>. A backend whose backend_get_env_dir() returns another directory needs its own backend_remove_env(). Without it, remove_env() aborts with condathis_remove_env_failed, whose parent has the class condathis_unsafe_env_dir_delete.

  • backend_available(backend) returns TRUE or FALSE: whether the backend can create environments on this system now. It must be cheap. It only decides which backend method = "auto" picks for a new environment. condathis still lists, finds and uses the existing environments of an unavailable backend. Default: TRUE.

  • backend_clean_cache(backend, verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full")) deletes the package caches and the metadata caches of the backend, and nothing else. It returns NULL when there was nothing to clean, or a result list (see Results). clean_cache() calls it for every registered backend, also after the function of another backend failed, and then deletes <root>/conda-pkgs itself. Default: NULL.

  • backend_quiesce(backend, timeout = 30) waits until no work of the backend runs in the R process any more, at most timeout seconds, and returns TRUE (invisibly), or FALSE with a warning when the time ran out. condathis calls it before with_sandbox_dir() and clean_cache() delete directories. An error from it, or a value other than TRUE or FALSE, becomes a warning of class condathis_backend_quiesce_failed, and condathis goes on. A backend that only starts processes has nothing to wait for. Default: TRUE.

  • backend_native_platform(backend) returns the platform (subdir) that the backend solves for when it gets no platform, such as "osx-arm64", or NA when it cannot tell. Default: NA.

  • backend_can_solve(backend, packages = NULL, env_file = NULL, channels = "conda-forge", channel_priority = c("strict", "flexible", "disabled"), additional_channels = NULL, platform) returns TRUE when the request solves for platform, FALSE when it does not, and NA when it cannot tell, for example without network access or for a missing channel. It must not create an environment. condathis asks it when it chooses the platform of a new environment. A request that does not solve for the native platform uses an emulated one when it solves there: "osx-64" on Apple Silicon with Rosetta 2, and "win-64" on Windows on ARM. An error counts as NA. Default: NA, so condathis never chooses an emulated platform. condathis never asks it about a lock (see backend_describe_definition()). It can also take the optional argument definition = NULL.

  • backend_describe_definition(backend, definition, platform = NULL) tells condathis what the backend makes of an env_definition(): whether it reads it, and whether it is a request or a lock. platform is the platform of create_env(). create_env() calls it before it locks, moves or creates anything, so it must be cheap: read the file, but do not download, install or solve anything, and do not change any environment. It returns a list:

    • supported: TRUE (the backend reads it), FALSE (it does not) or NA (it cannot tell). FALSE aborts with class condathis_create_env_unsupported_definition (also condathis_backend_unsupported), with reason in the message. Refuse an option of definition$options that you do not understand: never ignore it.

    • format: NA, or the name of the format that the backend detected or was given, such as "conda-lock-v1".

    • kind: "request" (the backend solves it, as package specs), "lock" (it installs exact packages, without a solve) or NA.

    • platforms: NULL, or the platforms that a lock has packages for.

    • reason: NA, or one sentence: why supported is FALSE.

    • records: NULL, or for a lock a data frame with the character columns name, version, build_string and platform (the platform the record is for), one row per package that the backend installs from it.

    For a request, condathis goes on as for package specs: it asks backend_can_solve() about the platform. For a lock, it picks the platform from platforms and never calls backend_can_solve(), since a dry run says nothing about a lock. It aborts when channels, additional_channels or channel_priority were given with an env_definition() (the deprecated env_file of create_env() passes them on, as in 0.1.4). Records of noarch packages install on any platform: leave noarch out of platforms. When records has rows for the platform and the new environment has no package, the create fails with condathis_create_env_failed. With NA as kind, condathis passes the file on and makes no other check, as for every backend before this function existed. An error counts as NA.

    records also lets condathis compare an existing environment with a lock: create_env(overwrite = FALSE) keeps the environment when its packages are exactly the records for the platform, and validate_env() gives TRUE. Records with NA in name, version or build_string are not compared. install_packages() calls this function too, and installs from a request only.

    With method = "auto", a new environment from a definition goes to the first available backend in condathis.backend_priority order whose supported is not FALSE. Default: NA, or FALSE when the definition has a format or options and backend_create_env() has no definition argument.

  • backend_definition_formats(backend) returns the names of the formats that the backend reads, as a character vector, such as c("environment-yaml", "explicit"). It is used only in messages: an error for a definition with a format names the registered backends that list it. condathis never decides from it. Default: character(0).

  • backend_resolve_run_in_dir(backend, cmd, args = character(0L), env_dir, verbose = "silent", base_env = NULL, timeout = Inf) describes how to run cmd with args in the activated environment whose directory (its prefix) is env_dir. This is an environment given by env_path(), which condathis did not create and which may belong to no backend, such as one made by conda or mamba elsewhere. It returns list(command, args, env, dir) with the rules of backend_resolve_run() (also for base_env and timeout). condathis treats the value the same way, also when it breaks them. It must not change, lock or register the environment. condathis calls it with activation on, after it checked that env_dir exists and has a conda-meta directory. It calls it only when the backend object has this function. For a backend without it, run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() abort with class condathis_env_path_unsupported_method (also condathis_backend_unsupported) when method names that backend. method = "auto" uses the first backend in the order of the option condathis.backend_priority that has it (micromamba by default). Default: aborts with class condathis_backend_unsupported.

Every value is checked: a return value that breaks these rules aborts with condathis_backend_invalid_return (also condathis_backend_contract_violation), naming the backend.

Results

backend_create_env(), backend_install(), backend_remove_env() and backend_clean_cache() may return NULL or a list. condathis copies the elements status, stdout, stderr, timeout, pid and cmd when present (exact names) and ignores everything else. Any other value counts as an empty list. A non-zero status without an error counts as a failure. cmd is reported as the command line that ran, so give the exact command line, or leave it out. condathis shows the password and the token of a URL in it as *****, as micromamba does. Hide them the same way in what the backend prints and in its errors.

The element link_scripts_skipped of the results of backend_create_env(), backend_install() and backend_remove_env(), when present, is a data frame with the character columns package and script ("pre-link", "post-link" or "pre-unlink"). It holds the link scripts of packages that the backend did not run. condathis then warns with class condathis_link_scripts_skipped after the call succeeded, naming the packages (see condathis-conditions). A backend that runs every link script, as micromamba does, leaves the element out. Any other value aborts with condathis_backend_invalid_return.

Missing environments

condathis checks with backend_env_exists() that an environment exists before it calls backend_install(), backend_remove_env(), backend_list_packages() and backend_resolve_run(). A missing environment aborts with class condathis_env_not_found before the backend is called. So these functions do not get a missing environment from condathis, except when backend_env_exists() failed. Then condathis calls them anyway, and they must signal an error for a missing environment. Give that error the class condathis_env_not_found. condathis keeps the condathis_* classes of a backend error when it re-raises it, so one handler catches a missing environment on both sides. None of them may create an environment.

Only run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() and install_packages() create a missing environment, and only the default "condathis-env": they call backend_create_env() for an empty environment first.

For a missing environment, backend_env_exists() returns FALSE, backend_list_envs() leaves the name out, and backend_get_env_dir() returns the path anyway. None of them signals an error for it.

Errors

Signal an error of any class when an operation fails. condathis re-raises it with your error as the parent, and with these classes:

  • condathis_<function>_failed, for example condathis_create_env_failed.

  • condathis_backend_error.

  • Every condathis_* class of your error.

Handlers still find your own classes with rlang::cnd_inherits().

When you cannot honor an argument, such as env_file or channel_priority = "flexible", also give your condition the class condathis_backend_unsupported.

Do not give your own conditions the class condathis_backend_error: condathis adds it when it re-raises your error. An error that has it anyway is re-raised like any other error.

An error from backend_env_exists() means "cannot tell", never "absent". A call that would change the environment then aborts with condathis_backend_probe_failed. A query warns with condathis_backend_query_failed and skips the backend.

See condathis-conditions for every class.

Channels

Search only the channels in channels and additional_channels, in that order, and no default channels. channel_priority has its Conda meaning. The channel column of backend_list_packages() is the channel name, as micromamba reports it (for example "conda-forge"), or the channel URL. condathis compares https://conda.anaconda.org/<name> equal to <name>, and drops credentials (user:password@, /t/<token>) and a platform subdirectory. It compares a file:// channel by its absolute path.

Child processes

condathis starts command with a copy of the session's environment in which the CONDA_* and MAMBA_* variables listed in condathis-options are cleared. It then applies env. For commands of every backend other than "micromamba", CONDA_ENVS_PATH is the parent directory of the environment directory from backend_get_env_dir(), so a Conda tool run in the environment creates named environments next to it. CONDA_PKGS_DIRS and MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS are <root>/conda-pkgs for them when that parent directory is <root>/envs, and "" otherwise. A Conda tool run in the environment keeps its package cache in the backend's root, never in the user's home directory or in the cache of another backend. clean_cache() empties it. For an environment given by env_path(), they have the values of the backend's own environments (those of "condathis-env"), not of the directory that holds it. The "micromamba" backend sets these variables to the envs/ and pkgs/ directories of its own root. A backend whose commands need other values returns them in env.

Registering from a backend package

Put condathis in Imports, so it is loaded before your package, and register from your package's .onLoad(). Also register from a hook on the condathis load event. The registry lives in the condathis namespace, so a registration is lost when condathis is unloaded and loaded again, as during development with pkgload::load_all(). The hook registers the backend on every later load of condathis. The hook list belongs to base R and outlives your package, so .onUnload() must remove the hook. Otherwise, the next load of condathis registers the functions of an unloaded namespace.

register_mybackend <- function(...) {
  condathis::register_backend("mybackend", new_backend_mybackend())
}

.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  register_mybackend()
  setHook(packageEvent("condathis", "onLoad"), register_mybackend)
  invisible(NULL)
}

.onUnload <- function(libpath) {
  hook <- packageEvent("condathis", "onLoad")
  setHook(
    hook,
    Filter(function(h) !identical(h, register_mybackend), getHook(hook)),
    action = "replace"
  )
  if (isNamespaceLoaded("condathis")) {
    condathis::unregister_backend("mybackend")
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

register_mybackend() must be a function at the top level of your package, so that identical() finds it. A function created inside .onLoad() is a new object every time. Call condathis functions with condathis:: instead of importing them in your NAMESPACE. After a reload of condathis, imported copies would be the functions of the old namespace.

register_backend() validates the backend, so after a condathis upgrade that changes the contract, the call in .onLoad() fails and your package does not load. The error names what to change. R runs the hook under try(), so a failing hook only prints its error and condathis still loads.

condathis knows some backend packages by name: rattlerthis provides the backend "rattler". condathis loads such a package when it is installed and one of these holds:

  • method names its backend.

  • Its backend has environments (a directory in <backend_root_dir(name)>/envs), so that method = "auto" finds them without a call to library().

  • The option condathis.backend_priority names its backend, and method = "auto" chooses the backend of a new environment.

condathis does not depend on these packages. When such a package is not installed, or fails to load, a method that names its backend aborts with class condathis_backend_not_installed or condathis_backend_load_failed. A change to one of its environments aborts the same way. The queries skip its environments with a warning of the same class (see condathis-conditions). The package must register its backend from its .onLoad(). A package that loads without registering it counts as failed.

See also

condathis-conditions for the condition classes, and condathis-options for the variables of child processes.

Other backends: backend_root_dir(), list_registered_backend_names(), unregister_backend()

Examples

# A minimal backend: the three required functions, which this example
# does not implement. It reports that it is unavailable, so
# `method = "auto"` never selects it. condathis supplies the other
# functions: they look for environments in
# `backend_root_dir("mybackend")/envs`. A backend package builds this
# object in its own constructor, for example `new_backend_mybackend()` in
# *Registering from a backend package* of `?register_backend`.
not_implemented <- function(...) {
  stop("Not implemented by this example backend.")
}
mybackend <- structure(
  list(
    backend_create_env = not_implemented,
    backend_install = not_implemented,
    backend_resolve_run = not_implemented,
    backend_available = function(backend) FALSE
  ),
  class = c("condathis_backend_mybackend", "condathis_backend")
)

condathis::register_backend("mybackend", mybackend)
condathis::list_registered_backend_names()
#> [1] "micromamba" "mybackend" 

condathis::unregister_backend("mybackend")
condathis::list_registered_backend_names()
#> [1] "micromamba"
